A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OmniSAM work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and supplementary materials are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original OmniSAM segmentation results across three adaptation scenarios, component ablations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original segmentation experiments and ablations and additionally reports total parameter counts and computational costs.

M1.justification: The SAM2/LoRA encoder, semantic decoder, memory mechanism, dynamic pseudo-label procedure and FPA objective remain unchanged. Section 3.4 clarifies target-model initialization from source weights without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Stanford2D3D-Pinhole, Stanford2D3D-Panoramic, Cityscapes, SynPASS and DensePASS for the same indoor Pin2Pan, outdoor Pin2Pan and outdoor Syn2Real scenarios, with unchanged category coverage.

E2.justification: Segmentation comparator membership in Tables 1–4 is unchanged. V2 adds a computational-cost comparison against Trans4PASS+-S, DATR-S and 360SFUDA++ in supplementary Table 7; this resource comparison was absent from v1.

E3.justification: The supplement changes DensePASS resizing and stride from 4096 × 1024/384 to 3072 × 1024/256. V2 Section 4.1 still specifies the earlier values, so this establishes conflicting reported settings rather than confirmed experimental reruns. The new computational-cost comparison specifies 1024 × 1024 inputs.

E4.justification: V2 adds analysis of how total model size and computational cost vary across OmniSAM variants and competing networks (supplementary Section 2.2). Existing component, memory-bank, pseudo-label and lambda ablations remain; the lambda analysis is moved to the supplement.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. The reporting of point estimates and learning curves is unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises the outdoor OmniSAM-T with MA row, including mIoU from 59.61 to 59.01. The indoor supplement changes Tiny results without/with MA from 67.84/68.26 to 68.72/69.10, matching unchanged Table 2. Several comparison deltas are corrected, and resource figures are added or revised. Headline best scores remain 79.06 and 62.46; conflicting preprocessing descriptions prevent interpreting the outdoor revision as a verified same-setting performance loss.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), prototype definitions and averaging, alignment assumptions and loss formulations are retained. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same first-application claim for SAM2 in panoramic semantic segmentation, the same three principal contributions and the same headline performance claims.

C2.justification: V2 newly acknowledges that the Base and Large variants' total model sizes may constrain real-time applications and require an inference-speed tradeoff. Existing interpretations of indoor adaptation and the Syn2Real limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 identifies the GPUs as NVIDIA A800 and explicitly states target-model initialization from source weights. It expands resource reporting and revises MB-labeled trainable sizes approximately fourfold, for example Large with MA from 25.41 to 6.35, without explaining the accounting change. The revised supplementary DensePASS preprocessing conflicts with the main text.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Deformable Mamba for Wide Field of View Segmentation, SGAT4PASS and Open Panoramic Segmentation. These modestly expand background coverage without substantially changing research positioning or novelty claims.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering remain intact. V2 expands an affiliation, adds acknowledgements, clarifies initialization, revises parameter discussion and relocates trainable-parameter discussion and the lambda ablation to the supplement.

P2.justification: V2 removes v1 Figure 1's radar summary, adds computational-cost Table 7 and moves the lambda table from the main text to supplementary Table 8. Other diagrams, visualizations and tables are largely retained with resizing, repositioning and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The new computational-cost comparison and real-time limitation improve transparency, while corrected indoor appendix rows resolve discrepancies with the main table. However, v2 introduces conflicting DensePASS preprocessing instructions and an unexplained fourfold revision of MB-labeled trainable sizes. These benefits and reproducibility ambiguities prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
